Spoilers First of all, the book series is nearly as old as I am and I only really learned about it a year ago. Something about the popularity of the show just struck me wrong "there's no way people actually like medieval stuff on HBO." But my inner man-child gave in when I learned that Sean Bean was in a suit of armor. I marathoned the first season and absolutely loved Sean's performance, he played a wonderful do-gooder. I figured all of the performances would be as exhilarating so I dropped the show and picked up the books. The first book roughly played out the same way as the first season so I finished the show, then went back to the books. What really hooked me on buying the books was this air of mystery and mysticism that's not really touched on in the show. The show just drops the set pieces in your lap and I figured it was because it was explained in-depth in the books. Boy was I wrong.

I can't imagine reading the first book in 96' that in my opinion, is the best of the series. It sets a wonderful tone and the seven kingdoms literally feels like a time bomb. Politically and socially the world is starting to fall apart and you have a feeling that something is about to happen. You know about the White Walkers immediately, the still living "Dragon", the incest.. but most of it is never resolved. GRRM loves to spend time developing characters that we may never hear from or see again. He's made so many tangents to the same story in order to smash them all together in the last few books, but honestly the story has started to dilute for me. There definitely seemed to be a one way path through all the bullshit in the first book but I have to remind myself that this series started with "Game of Thrones" and that's literally what it is.

Maybe my point here is there's almost no development after all the Stark chapters, unless somebody gets killed. Is the point of these books to represent how stupid and illogical the Game of Thrones is? With nearly 90% of the characters having ulterior motives you really are left to guess what the hell is going on. You are left reading about the people who always seem to be out of the loop and being beheaded by the people "in the loop". Every time you think a character is actually making some progress on what the hell this "loop" is they get offed. It was almost masterfully executed the FIRST time with Ned, but now... I'm trying to find a reason to care.

I may just watch the last season of a Game of Thrones and call it quits. The characters that book 1 and 2 hooked you on aren't going to see any closure until... wait for it... until GRRM writes his last book. And with all the promise of dragons and witches, little green forest people, Giants, Mammoths, Wargs, Glass candles, prophecies, rightful kings "mysticism" etc. that we haven't seen (mostly) you really (I really) find myself going "what the fuck have I been reading about for five books then?" Anybody else out there in the same boat?
I'm having a hard time feeling optimistic for the next book
